title: Common-stage compact support with canonical Weil structures
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with no equality imposed between the scheme and coefficient universes. For finite-type $k_0$-schemes use the actual common-stage constructible categories and the categories of geometric-Frobenius fixed pairs [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Use the geometric-fibre inverse image $P_f=f^*$ and its normalized Frobenius square $P_fF_X\simeq F_YP_f$ of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category].

For a proper morphism $p_0:X_0\to Y_0$, $P_p$ has a right adjoint $R_p$ on these common-stage constructible categories; choose it together with its adjunction. Define $e_p:R_pF_Y\to F_XR_p$ to be the right mate of the inverse normalized pullback square under $P_p\dashv R_p$. This mate is invertible. For an open immersion $j_0:X_0\to Y_0$, $P_j$ has a left adjoint $J_j$, chosen with its adjunction. Define $d_j:F_XJ_j\to J_jF_Y$ to be the left mate of the normalized pullback square under $J_j\dashv P_j$; it is invertible, and put $e_j=d_j^{-1}$. These adjunction universal properties determine the chosen operations up to unique compatible natural isomorphism; no arbitrary comparison is chosen.

For $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ and a compactification $c=(j_0,p_0)$, use the middle $k_0$-scheme and the two $k_0$-arrows constructed in [def-zl-weil-compact-support-cohomology]. Define $H_{f,c}=J_jR_p$ in diagrammatic functor order (first $J_j$, then $R_p$). Its Frobenius comparison $e_{f,c}:H_{f,c}F_Y\simeq F_XH_{f,c}$ is $J_j(e_p)$ followed by $e_jR_p$, with the ordinary associators. Define its functor on Weil fixed pairs by $(K,\theta)\mapsto(H_{f,c}K,e_{f,c,K};H_{f,c}(\theta))$ and by $H_{f,c}$ on underlying morphisms. For a separated finite-type $f_0$, for every geometric compactification $c_g$ and every normalized coefficient action $S$ [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action] on that compactification, $H_{f,c}$ is naturally isomorphic, on every object and morphism, to $S$'s common-stage functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Finally, for composable maps and chosen compactifications, define the Frobenius comparison of the iterated functor $H_fH_g$ by $H_f(e_g)$ followed by $e_fH_g$, with the associators.
